insight: Site EUI is heavily right-skewed; the log transform fixes it
evidence: Skewness 4.556 raw vs -1.114 logged; excess kurtosis 42.541 vs 5.223
consequence_for_modelling: log_EUI is the modelled response for RQ1-RQ4. Residual tails will stay heavier than normal, so RQ1 diagnostics are read against that expectation and inference uses design-based standard errors that assume neither normality nor equal variance.

insight: Floor-to-ceiling height carries a documented top-code, not an outlier
consequence_for_modelling: Capped at 50 ft with a separate top-code indicator, so the records inform the model without exerting leverage as 995-foot ceilings. Recoding rather than deletion preserves the JK2 replicate structure.

insight: Survey weights materially change the activity mix and are not optional
evidence: Service buildings are 5.49 percent of the sample but 15.43 percent of the weighted stock; offices fall from 20.91 to 17.29 percent
consequence_for_modelling: FINALWT anchors every population statement in RQ1 and RQ2. The predictive questions RQ3 and RQ4 are deliberately unweighted, because generalisation error is a property of the fitted function rather than a population parameter.

insight: Operating hours is the strongest single continuous correlate of energy use
evidence: r = 0.406 with log EUI, against 0.084 for floor area and 0.149 for workers
consequence_for_modelling: WKHRS enters every model. This is a zero-order association only; RQ1 tests whether it survives controlling for building activity, since long-hours activities such as food service are also energy-intensive.

insight: The two climate variables are strongly collinear with each other
evidence: r = -0.716 between heating and cooling degree days
consequence_for_modelling: Both are retained pending a variance inflation check in RQ1 rather than dropped pre-emptively, so that a heating coefficient distinct from a cooling coefficient remains interpretable if the diagnostic permits it.

insight: Workforce size is largely a restatement of floor area
evidence: corr(NWKER, SQFT) = 0.674; converting to density gives corr(density, ln_SQFT) = -0.107
consequence_for_modelling: Occupancy enters as worker density per 1,000 sq ft, not as a headcount. A raw count would reintroduce the very scale that the EUI response divides out and would inflate collinearity with the floor-area term.

insight: Building activity separates energy use more than any other variable
evidence: Survey-weighted typical EUI spans roughly 11 kBtu/sq ft/yr for vacant premises to 219 for food service, a twenty-fold range
consequence_for_modelling: RQ4 defines its low, medium and high bands as terciles within each activity rather than across the stock. An absolute tercile would reward a classifier for recovering the building type it was already given.

insight: Operating hours is bounded and piles up at the 168-hour ceiling
evidence: 1474 buildings report the full 168-hour week (23.2 percent of the sample)
consequence_for_modelling: OPEN24 is a deterministic restatement of WKHRS = 168, so the two carry the same information. RQ1 retains both only after confirming the variance inflation factors stay within tolerance.
